CVE-2026-103025.title: bep/imagemeta: Unbounded memory allocation decoding PNG `zTXt` "Raw profile type iptc" chunks
CVE-2026-103025.description: bep/imagemeta is a Go library for reading EXIF, IPTC and XMP image meta data from JPEG, TIFF, PNG, and WebP files. Prior to 0.17.3, imagemeta.Decode could exhaust memory when parsing PNG zTXt chunks whose keyword is "Raw profile type iptc": the declared chunk length can drive an allocation far larger than the input file, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output limit. The advisory reports a 42-byte input causing a 256 MB allocation and a 127 KB input inflating to 460 MB. The oversized-allocation path's memory effect depends on platform overcommit and configured GOMEMLIMIT or cgroup limits, while the decompression path reliably creates resident memory. Applications that decode untrusted PNGs with IPTC metadata processing can therefore suffer denial of service through memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in 0.17.3.

CVE-2026-123867.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a per-host mTLS authorization bypass via a CA-only SNI context failing open to the default CA
CVE-2026-123867.description: A per-host mutual-TLS authorization bypass in Node.js lets a client authorized for the default hostname reach a protected hostname it is not authorized for. When a TLS server assigns a hostname a different client-certificate CA with `server.addContext(host, { ca: protectedCA })` but no server certificate in that SNI context, the per-host client CA is never installed and the handshake falls back to the default client CA. In `src/crypto/crypto_tls.cc`, `CertCbDone` installs the SNI context's CA only when `setSniContext` succeeds, but `setSniContext` returns `false` for a context with no server certificate, so a CA-only SNI context silently keeps the default CA. A client holding a certificate trusted by the default CA, but not the protected CA, can therefore complete mTLS to the protected hostname and read its response even with `requestCert` and `rejectUnauthorized` enabled, while a client certified by the protected CA is rejected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

CVE-2026-99687.title: vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages
CVE-2026-99687.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

vhost-scsi: zero misaligned I/O bounce pages

The misaligned I/O fallback copies the full bounce scatterlist to the
request buffer during completion. If a data-in command transfers less
than requested, part of a newly allocated bounce page can remain unwritten.

Allocate bounce pages with __GFP_ZERO so all bytes copied during completion
have a defined value. This path is already the slow fallback for
misaligned I/O, so the added initialization cost is acceptable.

Found during an LLM-assisted source audit and validated with a QEMU/KVM
vhost-scsi target using misaligned data-in commands.
